successors.note: The page: Davaka "was probably absorbed into Kamarupa in the first half of the 5th century", during the reign of Kalyana Varman (422-446), as B. N. Puri and P. C. Choudhury claim. The kamarupa-kingdom dossier has the matching gain in 422 (its counterpart string is davaka).

capitals.name: Davaka (site near the Kopili river)
capitals.note: The page: "Its capital was located near Kopili river"; the infobox capital is unknown and the exact site is disputed (Dabaka in Hojai district against the Davaka region of Nagaon district). The coordinates are a stand-in for Hojai, not a page figure.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Davaka row. The page places the kingdom in the Kopili-Kolong valley (Hojai district, or the Davaka region of Nagaon district) and gives no area. The radius is the researcher's reading.

ledger.note: c. 350: Davaka appears as a frontier kingdom. The page dates it only by the Allahabad Pillar ("The references to it comes from the 4th century") and gives "??-6th century CE" in the infobox; 350 is a bridge to the mid-4th century of the inscription. A Davaka king sent an ambassador to China in 428 AD (after the end year used here).

ledger.note: c. 422: Kalyanavarman of Kamarupa absorbs Davaka. "absorbed much earlier in the first half of the 5th century during the reign of Kalyana Varman" (reign 422-446; Puri: "It is presumed that (Kalyana Varman) conquered Davaka"); the page records Davaka's embassy to China in 428, which does not fit an absorption before 428, and leaves the infobox end blank.

certainty.note: No border is given; the kingdom is a river valley named by the Allahabad Pillar as one of five frontier kingdoms.

sources.title: Davaka
sources.note: Period, capital near the Kopili river, the Allahabad Pillar, Kalyana Varman and Kamarupa.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (the kamarupa-kingdom dossier uses the counterpart davaka). One page opened (budget 2-5). The dates are bridges: 350 is the Allahabad Pillar's century, 422 is the start of Kalyana Varman's reign, but the page also has a Davaka king sending an ambassador to China in 428, so Davaka may have lasted to Kalyana Varman's later years or beyond. The page calls Davaka a Gupta "frontier kingdom" without describing a relationship; no vassal event is written. Gazetteer names needed: Davaka, Kopili valley (region).
